assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework fundamentally shaped modern monetary economics and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Calvo, Taylor and Woodford provide a coherent three-person account of price-setting, policy rules and the framework's theoretical synthesis.
assessment.maturity: Its central ideas have been tested, extended and used extensively over several decades.
uncertainties: The candidate encompasses a broad research programme with several additional major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity transformed trade theory and empirical work on selection, reallocation and welfare from trade.
assessment.attribution: Helpman, Melitz and Redding represent central theoretical development and extension of the programme.
assessment.maturity: The framework has produced a durable, extensive body of theoretical and empirical research.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between the core Melitz contribution and related heterogeneous-firm trade work remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM supplied widely used tools for addressing unobserved heterogeneity and endogeneity in economic data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond are tightly linked to the foundational estimators and their practical implementation.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been scrutinized for decades and remain standard across applied economics.
uncertainties: Widespread use does not eliminate concerns about weak instruments and specification-sensitive applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining provided an elegant, influential foundation for strategic bargaining theory.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is the unmistakable principal contributor to the canonical bargaining model.
assessment.maturity: The result is long established and has shaped theory and applications in markets and negotiations.
uncertainties: The longlist's broader grouping includes related contributors whose relation to a single prize formulation requires care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression made distributional heterogeneity accessible to rigorous econometric analysis and has had broad scientific influence.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the clear originators of the core method.
assessment.maturity: The method has a long record of theoretical development and use across economics and other fields.
uncertainties: The appropriate scope of a prize beyond the original method is less clear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how economists formulate credible conclusions when point identification is unsupported.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the field's central foundational figure; later work broadened and operationalized the approach.
assessment.maturity: The perspective is mature, with deep theoretical foundations and growing applied relevance.
uncertainties: The extent to which the prize should encompass subsequent moment-inequality methods is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-data research on mobility made intergenerational opportunity measurable at unprecedented scale and policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the linked research programme and its data infrastructure.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated substantial follow-on research and replication-oriented extensions.
uncertainties: The programme is comparatively recent, and causal interpretation of geographic mobility patterns remains debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and financial-accelerator mechanisms supplied core explanations for amplification of financial disturbances.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore anchor the collateral-constraint mechanism, while Gertler is central to the financial-accelerator formulation.
assessment.maturity: These mechanisms have been deeply incorporated into macro-finance theory and studied through multiple financial episodes.
uncertainties: The listed contributions include distinct but related mechanisms, making a unified attribution challenging.
